primary-content.note: Sourced from Tailwind's neutral-100 via var(--color-neutral-100). The one token that carries no warm hue, because it sits on green rather than on paper.

link-underline.note: Single-role. Exists only as a 2px text-decoration at 0.3em offset.

forest.note: Reverse-out sections only. Three occurrences in the codebase.

base-100.note: The neutral ramp is the project's own spine: base-content, then base-300, base-200, base-100 at the light end.

base-300.note: Every border and section rule in the system.

base-content.note: All text. Its /70, /65, /60, /40 and /15 mixes are the entire secondary-text and decoration scale — there is no separate muted token.

display.purpose: Full-viewport hero headlines only. Scales 3rem → 5.5rem across sm/md/lg. Italic on the home hero. Utility: hero-display.

headline.purpose: The h1 of an ordinary page. Utility: page-title.

section.purpose: Section h2s. Steps to 2.25rem at md. Utility: section-title.

title.purpose: Product names and category tile labels. card-title steps DOWN to 1.25rem at sm because grid cards narrow; tile-title does not.

body.purpose: Default copy. Prose pages step up to 1.125rem with leading-relaxed, capped at max-w-2xl. main p carries text-wrap: pretty.

label.purpose: Section category labels, footer column headings, the 'From' price prefix. Always at base-content/70. Utility: eyebrow.

typographyExtras.name: footer-line
typographyExtras.purpose: Address, opening hours — things the shop says, so serif.

typographyExtras.name: logo-wordmark
typographyExtras.purpose: The header lockup. The only place sans is allowed to be large.

shadows.name: admin-overflow-cue
shadows.purpose: Below lg on .admin-table-scroll: signals a compact admin table continues horizontally. Functional — the only structural shadow in the system.

shadows.name: lightbox-credit
shadows.purpose: Keeps the photographer credit legible over an arbitrary photograph in PhotoSwipe.

shadows.name: product-mark-backdrop
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the 'Favourite' mark sits ON the photograph via an 85%-opaque base-100 backdrop with a 2px blur and a hairline frame.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Every link, button and [role=button] state change: colour, background, border, text-decoration-color, opacity, box-shadow, transform.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Hero text arrival (.hero-reveal): opacity 0→1 and translateY(12px)→0, staggered by an inline --reveal-delay.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Hero photography (.hero-zoom): scale(1.06)→scale(1). Transform-only, so LCP timing is unaffected.

motion.name: image-hover
motion.purpose: Product card and category tile photography on group hover.

motion.name: tile-label-lift
motion.purpose: Category tile label rises and its arrow slides in on hover.

motion.name: shy-header
motion.purpose: The fixed header translates fully out of view on scroll-down, returns on scroll-up.

motion.name: loading-dim
motion.purpose: Body-level dim to 0.7 during a LiveView click or reconnect. The 400ms delay keeps sub-400ms socket flaps invisible; un-dim is immediate.

motion.name: submit-swap
motion.purpose: Label↔spinner swap on submit buttons. Under 300ms the spinner never appears, so fast submits look instant.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The press lands instantly; the release fades back over ease-standard. Modelled on the Nord Design System.

motion.name: no-transition-active
motion.purpose: Deliberate absence. Category-index and size-option active underlines snap with no transition — hover breathes, active is a fact.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: The typography and gutter breakpoint. Also drops the carousel focal-point effect.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Footer goes to four columns; admin table overflow cue disappears.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: The navigation breakpoint — desktop nav, sign-in and locale picker appear; below this they live in a drawer.

radiusTokens.name: --radius-field
radiusTokens.purpose: Inputs, selects, textareas, badges, tabs, buttons. Overridden from daisyUI's 0.25rem default — this is what makes the system square.

radiusTokens.name: --radius-box
radiusTokens.purpose: Dropdowns, modals, drawers, alerts, cards. Overridden from daisyUI's 0.5rem default.

radiusTokens.name: --radius-selector
radiusTokens.purpose: daisyUI default, kept deliberately. Shapes radios and checkboxes; a square radio reads as a checkbox, and the checkout fulfillment picker depends on the distinction.

spacingTokens.name: --header-height
spacingTokens.purpose: Height of the fixed site header.

spacingTokens.name: --header-clearance
spacingTokens.purpose: Top offset for the first block on a page, so it clears the fixed header. Used via sm:mt-(--header-clearance) / sm:pt-(--header-clearance).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The acting control. Square, unshadowed, sans. Sizing approximated from daisyUI's btn-lg for preview.

components.name: Nav Link (honey underline)

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Square, full-width, label above inside one click target. The right-inset slot reserves space for a spinner or a confirmation check so the value never slides when state arrives.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; font-family: 'Open Sans', sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { margin-bottom: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--color-base-content, oklch(22% 0.015 75)); } .ds-field-shell { position: relative; display: block; } .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 3rem; padding: 0 2.5rem 0 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--color-base-300, oklch(93.5% 0.012 75)); border-radius: 0; background: var(--color-base-100, oklch(99% 0.004 75)); color: var(--color-base-content, oklch(22% 0.015 75)); font-family: inherit; font-size: 1rem; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary, oklch(0.3684 0.0478 156.76)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-field-trailing { position: absolute; inset-block: 0; right: 0.75rem; display: flex; align-items: center; pointer-events: none; color: oklch(62% 0.13 150); }

components.name: Radio Card
components.description: Fulfillment and option picker. Square container, circular radio — the radio's roundness comes from --radius-selector, the one softness left in the system, because a square radio reads as a checkbox.

components.name: Product Card
components.description: There is no card. A link, an unframed figure on a cream bed, and two lines of type. The focus ring frames the whole card through a full-bleed ::after rather than outlining the text.

Midsummer Bouquet

From45,00 €
components.css: .ds-product-card { position: relative; isolation: isolate; display: block; text-decoration: none; color: var(--color-base-content, oklch(22% 0.015 75)); max-width: 18rem; } .ds-product-card::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 10; pointer-events: none; } .ds-product-card:focus-visible { outline: none; } .ds-product-card:focus-visible::after { border: 2px solid var(--color-primary, oklch(0.3684 0.0478 156.76)); } .ds-product-figure { position: relative; margin: 0 0 1rem; aspect-ratio: 4 / 5; overflow: hidden; background: var(--color-cream, oklch(95% 0.025 75)); border-radius: 0; } .ds-product-photo { width: 100%; height: 100%; background: linear-gradient(145deg, oklch(78% 0.09 60), oklch(52% 0.08 150)); transition: transform 700ms ease-out; } .ds-product-card:hover .ds-product-photo { transform: scale(1.04); } .ds-product-name { margin: 0 0 0.375rem; font-family: 'Crimson Text', serif; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.375; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: transparent; text-decoration-thickness: 2px; text-underline-offset: 0.3em; transition: text-decoration-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-product-card:hover .ds-product-name { text-decoration-color: var(--color-link-underline, oklch(81% 0.15 93)); } .ds-product-price { margin: 0; font-family: 'Crimson Text', serif; font-style: italic; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1; color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-base-content, oklch(22% 0.015 75)) 65%, transparent); } .ds-product-price .ds-eyebrow { margin-right: 0.25rem; font-family: 'Open Sans', sans-serif; font-style: normal; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.18em; }

components.name: Category Tile

components.css: .ds-tile { position: relative; display: block; overflow: hidden; height: 18rem; max-width: 22rem; border-radius: 0; text-decoration: none; } .ds-tile-photo { width: 100%; height: 100%; background: linear-gradient(150deg, oklch(70% 0.10 40), oklch(38% 0.07 150)); transition: transform 700ms ease-out; } .ds-tile:hover .ds-tile-photo { transform: scale(1.04); } .ds-tile-scrim { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: linear-gradient(to top, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.15), transparent); } .ds-tile-veil { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); opacity: 0; transition: opacity 500ms; } .ds-tile:hover .ds-tile-veil { opacity: 1; } .ds-tile-label { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 0.625rem; margin: 0; padding: 1.5rem; font-family: 'Crimson Text', serif; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.375; letter-spacing: 0.025em; color: #fff; transition: transform 500ms ease-out; } .ds-tile:hover .ds-tile-label { transform: translateY(-0.375rem); } .ds-tile-label svg { align-self: flex-end; margin-bottom: 0.4rem; transform: translateX(-0.25rem); opacity: 0; transition: transform 500ms ease-out, opacity 500ms ease-out; } .ds-tile:hover .ds-tile-label svg { transform: translateX(0); opacity: 1; } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary, oklch(0.3684 0.0478 156.76)); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Everything sits on warm oat paper. A single serif — Crimson Text — carries the voice, and its italic is the closest thing the system has to handwriting. Sections are separated by a one-pixel rule, never by a card, never by a shadow, never by a change of background unless that change means something. Photographs run to the edge of the container or past it, and the interface never frames them: no radius, no border, no drop shadow, no caption box. The page is paper; the flowers are the ink.

The whole palette lives in one warm family. Every neutral sits at hue ~75 — oat, cream, near-black — so nothing on screen reads as cold grey. Forest green appears only where a section needs to reverse out entirely, and the deep green primary appears only on the things that act. One amber-honey stroke does all the interactive work: a 2px underline at a 0.3em offset, and nothing else. It never becomes a fill, a badge, or a body colour.

Density is generous and editorial. Sections breathe at 5–9rem of vertical padding, headings balance their own line breaks, and body copy avoids orphans. Interaction is quiet and physical: hover underlines fade in rather than pop, presses land instantly with a 1px downward translate and an opacity dip, and the release fades back. Motion is used for arrival and for photography — a 700ms rise on hero text, a 7s settle on hero photographs — and almost nowhere else.
keyCharacteristics: Warm oat paper (hue ~75) under everything; no cold grey anywhere.
Serif for voice, sans for interface — an absolute split.
Square at the token level — --radius-field and --radius-box are 0; only radios stay soft.
Hairline rules instead of cards, panels, or elevation.
One honey underline is the entire interactive vocabulary.
Photographs are full-bleed and unframed; they carry the persuasion.
Flat by default; a shadow must carry information to exist.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every surface, text and border colour sits at hue 60–80 (paper) or hue ~150 (forest). A colour outside those two families is a defect unless it is a semantic status colour inside /admin.

rules.name: The Honey-Only Rule
rules.body: The amber accent exists as a 2px text-decoration and nothing else. Never a background, never a border, never a text colour, never a badge. Its scarcity is what makes an underline read as 'this responds to you'.

rules.name: The Opacity-Not-New-Token Rule
rules.body: Secondary text, dividers and decoration are produced by mixing base-content with transparency (/70, /65, /40, /15), not by adding grey tokens. Reach for an opacity step before proposing a new colour.

rules.name: The Serif-Sans Split Rule
rules.body: Serif is for what the shop says — headings, product names, prices, quotes, addresses, opening hours. Sans is for what the interface says about itself — eyebrows, buttons, nav, form labels, the wordmark. A serif button or a sans product name is a defect.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A section that needs a category label above its heading uses the eyebrow (0.75rem, 700, uppercase, 0.18em) at base-content/70. Never a smaller heading, never a coloured chip, never a pill.

rules.name: The Balanced Heading Rule
rules.body: Every display, headline, section and pull-quote utility carries text-balance. Body copy carries text-wrap: pretty. Neither is optional — Swedish and Finnish produce much longer strings than English, and unbalanced headings break first in those locales.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: Vertical separation between sections is a one-pixel border (not-last:border-b) in base-300. Do not introduce a card, a panel, a margin-only gap, or an alternating background to separate sections. A background change (cream, forest) is reserved for sections that are genuinely a different kind of thing.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Rule
rules.body: Photographs run to the container edge or past it. On mobile the carousel deliberately breaks out to the viewport edges (margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw)). Never frame a photograph with a border, a radius, a shadow, or a caption box.

rules.name: The Functional-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow must answer the question 'what would the user not know without this?' Overflow, floating layers and legibility over photography qualify. Cards, buttons, inputs, tiles and images do not.

rules.name: The Gradient-For-Legibility Rule
rules.body: Text over a photograph is made legible by a gradient scrim (from-black/50 via-black/15 to-transparent, bottom-up), never by a solid box, a blur panel or a shadow on the text.

rules.name: The Square Edge Rule
rules.body: Radius is 0, set at the token so nothing has to remember: the theme block pins daisyUI's --radius-field and --radius-box to 0. Exactly two exceptions exist: --radius-selector (kept at 0.5rem so radios stay circular) and rounded-full (things whose roundness is their meaning). rounded-full is the only radius utility in the entire codebase — nine of them. Any other radius in markup is a defect by construction.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px. If a boundary needs more weight than a hairline, it needs a different colour surface, not a thicker border.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: Every pressable control lands instantly: opacity 0.9, translate 0 1px, transition: none. The release fades back over 150ms. Do not add a scale, a ripple or a colour flash to a press.

rules.name: The Breathe-Don't-Pop Rule
rules.body: Hover underlines are permanently present and transparent; only their colour transitions in over 150ms. Active-state underlines snap with no transition. That difference is deliberate: hover is an invitation, active is a fact.

rules.name: The Orphan Rule
rules.body: A hand-written value that duplicates a token is a future defect. The old 0.25rem sites — radio card, checkout date-picker frame, admin warning banner, admin calendar cells, admin nav rounded-r, skip link — were all hand-matching daisyUI's --radius-field default. They were invisible until that token moved to 0, and then a radio card and the text input below it disagreed in the same checkout form. If you find yourself typing a value a token already sets, delete the value.

dos: Do set every new heading in Crimson Text and every new label, button and nav item in Open Sans. The split is absolute.
Do separate sections with not-last:border-b and reach for bg-cream or bg-forest only when the section is genuinely a different kind of thing.
Do let the radius tokens carry squareness. A component should need no radius utility at all; if you are typing one, the token is wrong or you are making an exception you have not justified.
Do express secondary text and decoration as opacity steps on base-content (/70, /65, /40, /15) rather than introducing grey tokens.
Do run photographs full-bleed and unframed, and make text over them legible with the bottom-up gradient scrim.
Do put text-balance on every serif heading and let main p handle body rag — Swedish and Finnish strings are materially longer than English and break first.
Do guard every new animation with @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), the way every existing one is.
Do give any visually-replaced control its focus ring back through :has(input:focus-visible), as the size picker does.
Do use --focus-color to recolour the focus ring when the default green would vanish against the surface, as the inverse button does over photography.
donts: Don't let the honey accent become anything other than a 2px underline at a 0.3em offset. No honey fills, borders, badges or text.
Don't add a shadow that does not answer 'what would the user not know without this?'. There is no elevation scale and none should be created.
Don't wrap content in a card, a panel or a bordered box to group it. Use a rule, a background family, or vertical space.
Don't introduce a colour outside hue 60–80 or hue ~150, except for semantic status colours inside /admin.
Don't drift toward the generic florist e-commerce template: no pastel pinks, script fonts, pill buttons, heart icons, soft drop shadows or stock bouquet photography.
Don't bring SaaS dashboard chrome onto the storefront: no cards-in-cards, no elevated panels, no gradient CTAs, no coloured status pills.
Don't reach for luxury-brand pastiche: no all-caps thin sans at large sizes, no black-and-gold, no borrowed-prestige letter-spacing. The wordmark is the only large sans in the system.
Don't add any radius utility except rounded-full. rounded-full is the only one left in the codebase, storefront and admin alike — that is the invariant, not a coincidence.
Don't transition an active state. Hover breathes; active snaps.
Don't square --radius-selector. Radios must stay circular.
Don't hand-write a value a token already sets. That is how the 0.25rem tier survived invisibly until the token under it moved.
